issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a function named make_y_state(circ, q, p), but the template defines create_y_state(...) instead (and its NotImplementedError message refers to make_y_state). This name/signature mismatch is structural and will confuse students (they will look for make_y_state as described in the tasks) and prevents direct integration with the provided solution and tests that reference make_y_state.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function create_y_state to make_y_state with the signature make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None (and update any docstrings/messages). Ensure the template's NotImplementedError and any references match the name used in the problem statement and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution implementation refer to the same helper for preparing a noisy |Y> resource state as make_y_state, but the template repository defines a function named create_y_state instead. This naming mismatch makes it unclear which function students are expected to implement and will cause confusion or test failures because tests and the problem text expect make_y_state while the starter code exposes create_y_state.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function create_y_state to make_y_state (or add a make_y_state wrapper that calls create_y_state) so the template, problem statement, and solution use the same identifier for preparing the noisy |Y> resource state.
